document_check.note: The source text is Kim D-H, 'Longitudinal Analysis of Amyloid PET and Brain MRI for Predicting Conversion from Mild Cognitive Impairment to Alzheimer's Disease: Findings from the ADNI Cohort', Tomography 2025;11:37, doi:10.3390/tomography11030037 (page 1). It is a retrospective analysis of 180 MCI patients from ADNI 2 and GO, 76 of them converters, in which each imaging index (SUVR, AV-45 BASS, MRI BAI and the composite shape feature) is assessed by univariable ROC analysis. The baseline shape feature AUC is 0.891 (0.836 to 0.933), with sensitivity 0.79 and specificity 0.87 at threshold 1.60 (Table 2, page 7). This matches the cited 'imaging-based conversion analysis (Kim 2025, P-1214)' and the existing record's cited_result. I read the whole text through to the References (page 14).

cited_result: Principal result: prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion within 6 years by the baseline composite imaging 'shape feature' (AV-45 BASS multiplied by MRI BAI), AUC 0.891 (95% CI 0.836 to 0.933), with sensitivity 0.79 and specificity 0.87 at a Youden-derived cut-off of 1.60. The review cites the fact that this conversion predictor includes no medication covariate.
tool_reason: The cited result is how well one baseline imaging measure (the composite shape feature) predicts later conversion from MCI, with no multivariable model fitted. Clarification 2 of the operator's 2026-09-29 review assigns a baseline measure evaluated as a predictor of later progression to QUIPS as a prognostic factor, even though it is reported as a ROC AUC, and not to QUADAS-2.

domains.rationale: The source population (ADNI 2 and GO) and the baseline sample (Table 1) are described. But the sample was chosen on data collected after baseline: repeat PET and MRI at 2 years. No recruitment period is given, and the flowchart (Figure A1) is an image that the text does not reproduce. The only counts given (Table A1: 295 excluded, 244 included) do not reconcile with the 180 analysed, so the proportion of eligible patients who took part cannot be worked out. The author acknowledges that the ADNI sample may be selected. The outcome-dependent exclusion is judged under attrition (domain 2).

domains.rationale: Patients lost before 6 years were excluded only if they had not converted. Converters were kept whenever their conversion occurred, and non-converters were kept only if they completed 6 years. The analysis is a binary ROC, not a time-to-event analysis, so this exclusion depends on the outcome and can distort the association between the factor and the outcome. Table A1 suggests that more patients were excluded (295) than included (244). No reasons for loss are given, and no attempt to recover outcome data is described. Excluded and included patients are compared only on demographics and baseline CDR, not on the prognostic factor, and they differ in age.

domains.rationale: The shape feature is defined (BASS multiplied by BAI), was measured from ADNI-preprocessed baseline images by the same semiautomatic procedure for all patients, and was available for everyone (complete-case by design). However, no reliability or reproducibility data are reported for this new index; its validity rests on the author's own earlier work [17]. The document does not say whether the analyst was blind to conversion status. The Methods expand BAI as 'brain atrophic index' while figure and table footnotes call it 'brain amyloid index'. The reported sensitivity and specificity use a cut-off chosen in the same data, although the AUC treats the factor as continuous.

domains.rationale: The outcome is labelled conversion to AD but is defined only by a global CDR threshold, and no diagnostic criteria for AD are described. Read literally, the threshold ('exceeded 1') means CDR 2, which does not fit the label or the 42% conversion rate. The CDR is a standard instrument applied to all patients under the ADNI protocol. Nothing is reported on whether CDR raters knew the imaging results, so differential misclassification cannot be excluded. The unclear definition combined with no information on blinding gives moderate risk.

domains.rationale: Known prognostic factors were measured and differed between converters and non-converters: age (73.1 against 68.7 years), APOE4 carriage and baseline diagnosis (LMCI 63% against 24%). None was accounted for, either in the design (EMCI and LMCI were pooled, with no matching or stratification) or in the analysis (univariable ROC and t-tests only). Medication was not measured: the body text never mentions any drug or treatment. The shape feature's discrimination therefore cannot be separated from age, disease stage or treatment. The study presents the index as a validated predictor of risk, not as an exploratory association, so confounding is relevant and the risk is high.

domains.rationale: Univariable ROC analysis suits the discrimination of one continuous factor. All four indices are reported at both time points, including the non-significant baseline difference from SUVR, so selective reporting is not evident, although no protocol is cited. But the cut-off, sensitivity and specificity were derived and evaluated in the same 180 patients with no validation, despite an objective to 'identify and validate'. No time-to-event method is used, although follow-up varied. Every 'Youden's J' in Table 2 exceeds 1 (1.65 for the shape feature) and equals sensitivity plus specificity, so the minus 1 was omitted. The participant counts do not reconcile (244 against 180).

overall: High risk of bias (QUIPS: high for study attrition and study confounding; moderate for study participation, prognostic factor measurement, outcome measurement, and statistical analysis and reporting).
overall_rationale: By the QUIPS rule, any high domain makes the overall rating high. Here two domains are high and four are moderate. Attrition is high because non-converters lost before 6 years were excluded while converters were kept, which is an outcome-dependent exclusion in a binary analysis with no time-to-event method, and no reasons for loss are given. Confounding is high because age, APOE4 and baseline diagnosis differed between groups but none was adjusted for, and medication was not measured. The overall rating would still be high if confounding were judged moderate, because the attrition finding is enough on its own.

tool_changed_2026_09_29.why: re-screen under the operator's clarified rules: The cited result is the baseline composite imaging 'shape feature' (a fixed product of AV-45 BASS and MRI BAI, with no fitted weights) evaluated as a predictor of conversion from MCI to AD within 6 years in an ADNI cohort: AUC 0.891 at baseline, with sensitivity and specificity at a cut-off set by Youden's J. The abstract says the study 'aimed to investigate the predictive power' of these biomarkers. This is a baseline measure evaluated for later progression, so clarification 2 makes it a prognostic factor and QUIPS applies, not QUADAS-2. PROBAST does not apply either, because no multivariable model is fitted, as the record itself notes.
